text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

The panel's composition can't plausibly have worked against you here: you and the successful candidate are both men, as were all four panellists. An all-male panel is worth noting as an institutional issue — it raises questions about the hospital's recruitment practices generally — but it isn't evidence of bias against *you*, and raising it would likely read as grasping, undermining the stronger points you have.

Your real grievance is substantive: a PhD and eight years running a section versus a master's and a management course. "Broad leadership experience" is vague and worth testing. Focus on that, and chase the written explanation — the two-week silence is the concrete failing. Resend in writing, cite any applicable policy or statutory deadline, and copy HR.
